title: Principle 9: Experimentation: Explore outside your comfort zone
coreMove: Test a meaningful alternative to the default method when comfort stops revealing new information.
sourcePressure: Experimentation pushes beyond default methods and comfort-zone habits while staying tied to the real skill. The source sidecar contains no named people, studies, institutions, places, dates, or artifacts for this chapter, so named source anchors must be omitted rather than invented.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Changing methods randomly, chasing novelty, or assuming discomfort proves improvement.

hook: Ch12: learner stares at browser tabs and realizes motivation is not enough
Ch12: broad modern world pressure opener
counterintuition: The obvious move is not the real move

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: Lucy, a newsroom editor testing a new fact-checking workflow
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next month produces visible evidence or another private feeling of effort
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lucy tests a new fact-checking workflow on one article and compares error catches against the newsroom default.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a marked-up article proof beside a red fact-check stamp

exampleSpecs.domain: Luke, a medical student comparing two study methods on the same anatomy block
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a deadline exposes the weakness early enough to adjust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Luke studies the same anatomy block with two methods and lets the recall score, not comfort, choose tomorrow's plan.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two anatomy diagrams separated by a folded index card

exampleSpecs.domain: Hugo, a swimming coach using a plateau to test a different stroke cue
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the learner keeps credibility with a reviewer, client, teacher, or team
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hugo treats a swimming plateau as a cue to test one stroke change for three timed laps.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a damp lap card clipped to the pool lane rope

exampleSpecs.domain: Paula, a researcher scheduling one serious method comparison
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the project survives contact with a real schedule and real standards
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Paula schedules one serious method comparison in the lab instead of filling the week with familiar repetitions.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two labeled sample trays on opposite sides of a lab bench

exampleSpecs.domain: Aman, a call-center trainer trying an uncomfortable live-call practice
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether comfort keeps protecting the exact skill gap that matters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aman takes the uncomfortable live-call practice because the script drills stopped revealing the trainee's real weakness.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a call-center headset resting on a printed script

exampleSpecs.domain: Kasia, a game designer stopping random method changes and tying tests to playability
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next attempt changes the skill instead of decorating the plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kasia stops changing game-design methods at random and ties the next test to one measurable playability problem.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a playtest note beside a controller with a loose thumbstick

skillTargets: test a bounded alternative to the default method
use plateau as a signal for experimentation
separate useful discomfort from random novelty

tryThisNowSpec: Change one practice variable for the next session and write what result would make you keep or reject the change.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
